summary:
Red Horizon: Junior Astronaut Mission
Every Choice Counts. Every Decision Teaches.

Red Horizon: Junior Astronaut Mission is a browser-based interactive educational game designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to space science and the challenges of human exploration on Mars.

Set in a fictional Mars research base in 2045, players take on the role of a Junior Mission Commander responsible for guiding astronauts through three missions involving solar storms, power shortages and greenhouse emergencies.

Guided by ASTRO, a friendly robot companion, players make decisions, experience their consequences and learn scientific concepts through interactive storytelling and resource management. By managing limited Power, Water and Food supplies, players develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills while discovering the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars.

The project aims to make space science more engaging and accessible to young learners through storytelling, problem-solving and educational activities. It encourages curiosity, critical thinking and responsible decision-making while introducing real-world space science concepts through NASA-related resources.
details:
1. Project Overview

Red Horizon: Junior Astronaut Mission is an educational game that introduces children to the challenges of living and working on Mars. Players become Junior Mission Commanders and make decisions to keep a fictional Mars research base operational.

The game is guided by ASTRO, a friendly robot companion who introduces challenges, explains situations and provides feedback after each decision.

2. Gameplay and Features

The game consists of three missions:

  • Solar Storm Alert: Players learn about solar storms and radiation protection.
  • Power Shortage: Players learn how Martian dust affects solar panels and electricity generation.
  • Greenhouse Emergency: Players learn about water conservation and plant growth.

Each mission presents two choices with different consequences. After making a decision, players receive a popup message from ASTRO explaining the outcome and showing which resource has decreased.

After completing all three missions, players receive a final mission completion screen displaying their remaining resources.

3. Resource Management System

A central gameplay mechanic is the resource management system, which requires players to balance three essential resources:

  • Power: Electricity available for the Mars base and its equipment.
  • Water: Water needed by astronauts and greenhouse plants.
  • Food: Food supplies available for astronauts.

Each resource begins at 100%, and player decisions influence the available resource levels. Resource changes carry forward between missions, allowing earlier decisions to affect subsequent challenges.

This interconnected system introduces the concept of resource trade-offs. A decision that improves one aspect of mission safety or operations may reduce the availability of another essential resource.

As a result, players must evaluate potential consequences, prioritise needs and consider the long-term sustainability of the Mars base rather than focusing solely on immediate solutions.

4. Educational Objectives

The game aims to help children:

  • Understand basic space science concepts related to Mars exploration.
  • Learn about solar storms, radiation, electricity and plant growth.
  • Recognise the importance of conserving limited resources.
  • Develop critical thinking and decision-making skills.
  • Improve problem-solving abilities through interactive scenarios.

5. Creativity and Innovation

Red Horizon combines educational storytelling, interactive decision-making and resource management to create an engaging learning experience.

Rather than presenting scientific information through conventional reading materials or static quizzes, the game places children in the role of mission commanders, allowing them to experience simplified space exploration challenges and learn through the consequences of their decisions.

One of its distinctive features is ASTRO, a robot companion who guides players throughout the mission. ASTRO communicates through contextual dialogue, situation-based facial expressions and feedback that responds to the player's decisions. This character-driven approach makes scientific explanations more approachable and helps maintain engagement throughout the experience.

Additionally, the interconnected resource system introduces meaningful decision-making. Players discover that there is not always one universally correct choice, as each decision involves balancing priorities, limitations and potential consequences.

By combining scientific concepts with interactive gameplay, Red Horizon aims to turn space exploration education into an experience where children actively participate, experiment and learn.

6. Tools and Technologies

The game was developed using a combination of web technologies, project management tools and AI-assisted development tools:

  • HTML: Used to structure the game's content and interface.
  • CSS: Used to design the game's layout, appearance and visual elements.
  • JavaScript: Used to implement interactive gameplay, mission logic, player choices and resource management.
  • GitHub: Used for source code management, version control and team collaboration.
  • ChatGPT: Used to support brainstorming, content development and coding assistance.
  • Gemini: Used as an AI-assisted tool for research, idea development and problem-solving.
  • Claude: Used to support coding, reviewing and refining parts of the game.

7. Scientific and Educational References

The project uses the following resources to support its educational content:

  • NASA DONKI: Information about solar events and space weather.
  • NASA Mars Trek: Mars imagery and geographical exploration.
  • NASA Open Science Data Repository: Scientific research data related to space biology.
  • Canadian Space Agency Food Production Toolkit: Educational information about food production and growing plants.

8. Intended Impact

Red Horizon aims to encourage children's curiosity about space exploration and STEM subjects. Through interactive storytelling and resource management, the game introduces the importance of scientific knowledge, critical thinking and responsible resource use in sustaining human life beyond Earth.
